headline: Peptide ADMET databases and multimodal predictors emerge alongside audit-ready evaluation standards
label: Peptide Admet Resources And Evaluation
summary: New peptide ADMET resources and models arrive as evaluation work questions leakage and exposure-blind ranking in drug prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is peptide pharmacology: ADMETatlas aggregates peptide ADMET evidence, motivated by permeability and in vivo stability as clinical bottlenecks, and Pepti-DrugPhAI jointly models SMILES and amino acid sequences to predict ADMET properties and toxicity. Adjacent items concern evaluation rigor rather than peptides. A perspective proposes an L0-L5 cold-start framework and leakage checklist for DDI/DTI models, a PBPK study shows dose-driven exposure and safety limits reorder generated PARP1 candidates, and patient-derived organoid screens supply benchmarking data for drug response models. What is new is pairing peptide-specific evidence and multimodal prediction with explicit, auditable evaluation, constraining how performance claims across such tools can be compared.
